title: Scheduling and causal: block classification, persistent, LPT ordering

steps.title: Causal block classification: split the main loop into an unmasked segment and a masked tail segment
Persistent: grid = SM count, static round-robin scheduling, barrier phases continue across tiles

cases.name: n1
cases.purpose: N=1: one CTA, two Q tiles; all 128 rows of tile 1 are out of bounds (TMA fills zeros, store skips them); O = V, LSE = scale·q·k.

cases.name: one_block
cases.purpose: N=128: only tile 0 is valid, B>1, H>1: coordinates of the 4-D tensor map and the grid mapping.

cases.name: two_tiles
cases.purpose: N=256 is exactly one tile pair, two K/V blocks, D=128: tile 1's Q coordinate (q0+128), the TMEM columns of S¹/O¹, the location of P¹.

cases.name: tile1_tail
cases.purpose: N=200: tile 1 has only 72 valid rows; the second K/V block has only 72 valid keys.

cases.name: tile1_position
cases.purpose: Non-causal, D=128, N=190: tile 1 has only 62 rows; V[j]=j/N exposes the packing order of P¹ (two adjacent keys swapped) and the TMEM columns of P¹.

cases.name: short_tail
cases.purpose: N=37, D=128: one row spans two 64-column panels; the 91 padding keys must be masked.

cases.name: scale
cases.purpose: scale=1, logits in the hundreds: scale must come from p.scale; without subtracting the max it overflows.

cases.name: uniform
cases.purpose: Q=0: O is the mean of V, LSE = ln N. Missing or doubled α or ℓ corrections show up.

cases.name: ones_v
cases.purpose: V=1, 5 blocks, 3 CTA rows (tile pairs): the O correction and the ℓ correction must use the same α for O to equal 1; P of padding keys must be 0.

cases.name: position
cases.purpose: V[j]=j/N, 5 blocks: a wrong item index (K even, V odd) or parity in the K/V ring buffer reads another block.

cases.name: peaked
cases.purpose: D=128, 7 blocks, large logits: the max updates repeatedly; the O correction (α) must finish before PV.

cases.name: peaked_d64
cases.purpose: D=64, FP16: N=513 is 1 more than a multiple of the block size; the TMEM columns of O¹ depend on D.

cases.name: ring
cases.purpose: 12 blocks, 24 ring items: the ring buffer wraps many times; a wrong full/empty parity reads an old block or hangs.

cases.name: peaked_fp16
cases.purpose: FP16, D=128, large logits and scale=1: for many elements x = (s − m)·scale·log₂e is far below −127, so the software exp2 must clamp to −127 first; the max jumps often in the first few blocks.

cases.name: growing
cases.purpose: The max grows slowly by about 1.4–4.3 (log₂ units) per block; each single-block increase is below τ, but the total is far above τ: the conditional rescale must compare with the "current reference", not with the previous block's max, or P exceeds the FP16 upper bound and becomes inf.

cases.name: growing_causal
cases.purpose: growing_max, causal, D=64: the max of each row grows in different blocks, so within one warp some rows need correction and some do not (warp vote).

cases.name: jump
cases.purpose: From key 650 (the middle of block 5) the logits jump up by about 145–430 (log₂ units): the jump block must move the reference and correct O (α ≈ 0), or P overflows to inf.

cases.name: jump_causal
cases.purpose: jump_max, BF16, causal, D=128: the jump starts at key 434; above 2^128 even BF16/FP32 overflows; rows before 434 do not see the jump, so inside a tile some rows jump and some do not.

cases.name: medium
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, D=128: the full ping-pong over 8 blocks.

cases.name: medium_d64
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, D=64, FP16.

cases.name: causal_n1
cases.purpose: Causal and N=1: the only query sees only itself.

cases.name: causal_pair
cases.purpose: Causal, one tile pair, large logits: block 2 of tile 0 is fully masked (must not produce NaN); the diagonal block of tile 1 needs a mask.

cases.name: causal_tail
cases.purpose: Causal and N not a multiple of the block size: the diagonal mask and the tail mask apply at the same time; the second tile pair has only 44 rows.

cases.name: causal_n_bound
cases.purpose: Causal, N=640: the block count of the last tile pair (rows 512..767) is set by N (5 blocks), not by the diagonal (6 blocks); tile 1 of that pair is fully out of bounds, and the last block of tile 0 has both the diagonal mask and the tail mask.

cases.name: causal_position
cases.purpose: Causal, V[j]=j/N, D=128: a mask that is off by one reads the value of a future position.

cases.name: causal_peaked
cases.purpose: Causal and large logits: masked elements in the diagonal block must not take part in the max.

cases.name: causal_uniform
cases.purpose: Causal and Q=0: O[i] is the mean of V[0..i], LSE[i] = ln(i+1).

cases.name: causal_ones_v
cases.purpose: Causal and V=1: O must equal 1, including row 0, which has only one key.

cases.name: causal_medium
cases.purpose: Medium-size causal, D=128: tile pair p processes only blocks 0..2p+1.

cases.name: causal_medium_d64
cases.purpose: Medium-size causal, D=64.

cases.name: bh1_causal
cases.purpose: B·H=1, causal: only 8 tile pairs, grid smaller than the SM count; the work is 2, 4, …, 16 blocks, an 8× spread.

cases.name: bh1_long
cases.purpose: B·H=1, non-causal, N not a multiple of 256: 6 tile pairs; the last pair has only 184 rows.

cases.name: uneven_causal
cases.purpose: Very uneven causal: 16 tile pairs per head, work 2..32 blocks; LPT reverses the index, so a wrong pair coordinate reads another position.

cases.name: multi_tile
cases.purpose: Tile count 450 = 3·148 + 6, not a multiple of the SM count: the first 6 CTAs do 4 tiles and the rest do 3; each CTA's tiles come from different batches/heads, the N tail and the diagonal mask appear together, and barrier phases continue across tiles.

cases.name: multi_tile_d128
cases.purpose: Non-causal, D=128, 480 tiles (3.2 rounds): Q/O reuse the same shared memory, and the epilogue must finish reading O's TMEM before the next tile overwrites it; V=1 makes any O that leaks into another tile deviate from 1.

cases.name: multi_tile_causal
cases.purpose: Causal, D=128, 640 tiles, jump_max: the conditional rescale state (m, ℓ) must be reset at the start of each tile, not carried over from the previous tile.

cases.name: many_one_block
cases.purpose: N=128: 2000 tiles with only 1 block each, 13–14 per CTA. Softmax writes the final m, ℓ of the next tile depending only on S_0, without going through correction, so it can run one tile ahead of correction: if final_full is not double-buffered by tile parity, it completes two phases in a row (hang); missing the q_empty commit in the prologue also hangs.

cases.name: perf
cases.purpose: B·H=64, N=4096, D=128: 550 GFLOP, the same case as labs 22 and 34.

cases.name: perf_causal
cases.purpose: B·H=64, N=4096 causal: 1024 tiles, 2..32 blocks per tile pair.

cases.name: perf_d64
cases.purpose: D=64, FP16: the MMA per key is halved, so the exponential (MUFU) takes a larger share.

cases.name: perf_8k
cases.purpose: N=8192, D=128: 64 blocks per CTA; the main loop dominates and the prologue and wind-down matter least.

cases.name: perf_causal_bh16
cases.purpose: Causal, B·H=16, N=8192: 512 tiles; the heaviest tile (64 blocks) is 2× the average, and the tile count is only 3.5× the SM count: the scheduling order decides the tail.
